newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity falls, April COB hits new low.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity falls, April COB hits new low.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures fell Thursday with California Oregon Border (COB) front months hitting new lows on fundamental weakness from warmer spring weather and expected abundant hydroelectric supplies, industry sources said.

As of 1210 EST, April California Oregon Border (COB) was trading down 38 cents at $9.00 per megawatt hour after hitting a new contract low of $8.85 per MWh, while May COB was trading down 25 cents at $9.15 after hitting a new contract low of $9.00 per MWh.
Summer deferreds were also showing weakness, with August trading down 20 cents at $17.10 after hitting a new contract low of $16.90 per MWh.

"There isn't any strength across the whole board," said one New York based futures trader, who said the market was fundamentally weak due to expectations of above-normal inexpensive hydroelectric generation this spring and into summer in California and the Pacific Northwest.
The warmer spring weather of April was also expected to minimize power demand, the trader said.
As of 1230 EST, April Palo Verde (PV) was steady at $12.90 after trading as low as $12.75 per MWh, while May was down 10 cents at $13.65 per MWh after reaching as low as $13.60 per MWh.
PV deferreds were also lower, with July trading down 50 cents at a new contract low of $19.45 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1210 an estimated total of 153 COB and 124 PV contracts had traded.
As of 1230 EST, NYMEX April Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading down 4.4 cents at $1.83 per million British thermal units.
In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to average near to slightly below normal through early next week, with showers and upper elevation snows likely for Saturday through Tuesday.

In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to be below normal through Sunday, then were called to rebound to slightly above normal Monday and Tuesday. Precipitation will average above normal through Sunday, with showers and mountain snows likely.
